title.narrative: Strengthening the capacities of indigenous Guaraní communities for the co-management of protected areas in Bolivia

description.narrative: Bolivia’s Gran Chaco region consists of swamps, salt flats, scrublands, and the largest un-touched dry forest on earth. This area plays an important role in the water supply of the indigenous Guaraní and Campesino communities. Despite the legal protection status of the newly established protected areas, they are increasingly threatened by agricultural activities, cattle ranching, and extensive fires. The project worked towards the effective co-management of these areas at the community level. This contributed to the conservation and sustainable management of the ecosystem services and the biodiversity found in the Bolivian Gran Chaco. Additionally, it strengthened the livelihoods of local communities under climate change conditions and helped to secure their access to natural resources.
